subject: FintechCo pricing follow-up: US vs EU residency impact & target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — post-demo recap & pricing follow-up

Quick recap from today's discovery with FintechCo (Alice + Rajesh):

- They currently proxy ~200M tokens/mo (primarily embeddings + chat rerank) and expect 1.5B tokens/mo within 12 months if performance and cost line up.
- Target budget range they mentioned in call: $50k–$90k/month initially (pilot) with potential to scale to $200k+/month. They asked specifically for target $/1M tokens we could support.
- Residency requirement: EU data-residency for EU customers (primary constraint), US residency for US customers. They want to understand the incremental cost on EU-resident data and any egress/region pricing delta.
- Technical notes: QPS spikes during batch settlement windows; prefix caching could reduce active token counts by ~20–30%.

Action items for us:
1) Validate unit economics: ballpark $/1M token ranges for reserved vs on-demand for both US and EU (include quantization/variant options).
2) Put together 3 pricing scenarios (pilot: 50M/mo, mid: 200M/mo, scale: 1.5B/mo) and show monthly cost and recommended reserved capacity commitments.
3) Confirm any EU premium (region-based infra + data residency) and call out egress or compliance costs.

I attached the working pricing-model.xlsx — please populate with assumptions and a simple per-1M token line so we can share to Alice.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo recap & pricing follow-up

Thanks — quick pass on numbers (high level). I updated pricing-model.xlsx (attached). Key assumptions included:

- Baseline unit (hosted on-demand): $1,800 / 1M tokens (US) for the model class they're targeting.
- Reserved / committed (monthly) discounts: 20% at 6-month commit, 30% at 12-month commit.
- EU premium: +20% on hosted rates to account for higher regional infra costs and data residency (so ~ $2,160 / 1M tokens on-demand).
- Quantization/runtime optimizations can reduce runtime cost by 10–25% depending on quality requirements — call this out as a technical lever.

Scenarios (rounded):
- Pilot (50M/mo): US on-demand equivalent ~$90k/mo; EU on-demand ~$108k/mo. With 6m reserved, pilot could be ~$72k (US) / ~$86k (EU).
- Mid (200M/mo): US on-demand ~$360k/mo; recommended reserved at 6–12m for 20–30% savings.
- Scale (1.5B/mo): we'd push dedicated capacity — per-1M economics improve substantially with dedicated pools and batching.

Open questions for Alice:
- Confirm whether data must be ingested and stored in EU for EU customers or if transient processing in EU is sufficient (this materially affects egress and storage fees).
- Any formal procurement timelines or thresholds for a reserved-commit purchase?

I left a few comments in the sheet. Happy to jump on a short call with Alice next week to walk through.

—Dylan
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo recap & pricing follow-up

Thanks Marissa / Dylan — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: For EU customers we require that customer data (both at-rest and processing) remain in EU regions. Transient processing outside EU is a non-starter for some of our customers (legal/compliance).
- Current volumes: ~200M tokens/mo (global). Our growth plan assumes 4–6x within 12 months as we onboard new enterprise customers in EU.
- Budget: For the pilot we can commit to ~$60k–$80k/mo. If the unit economics work, we'll scale commit levels.
- Unit economics ask: can you provide a target or a band for $/1M tokens we should expect for reserved vs on-demand in both US and EU? Also please highlight which levers (caching, batching, quantization) give the biggest delta.

Would like a short pricing summary we can share with procurement — ideally a 1-page table showing US vs EU per-1M, pilot vs reserved pricing, and any setup/one-time fees.

Best,
Alice Turner
Head of Platform & Integrations
FintechCo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — post-demo recap & pricing follow-up

Alice — thanks for the clarifications. Below is a concise pricing summary you can share with procurement (high level). I've attached a cleaned "pricing-model.xlsx" and a short SOW draft for pilot scope.

1) Headline per-1M token ranges (model class discussed):
   - US (hosted on-demand): $1,800 / 1M tokens
   - EU (hosted on-demand w/ EU residency): $2,160 / 1M tokens (+20% regional premium)

2) Reserved pricing (recommended for predictable workloads):
   - 6mo commit: ~20% discount (US: $1,440 / 1M; EU: $1,728 / 1M)
   - 12mo commit: ~30% discount (US: $1,260 / 1M; EU: $1,638 / 1M)

3) Pilot recommendation (to fit your $60k–$80k/month band):
   - Pilot volume: 50M tokens/mo
   - Option A (US-focused pilot): 50M * $1,440/1M (6mo reserved) = ~$72k/mo
   - Option B (EU-resident pilot): 50M * $1,728/1M (6mo reserved) = ~$86.4k/mo

4) Levers and expected delta:
   - Prefix caching / KV caching: expect ~15–30% reduction in billable tokens for rerank/prompt-heavy workloads
   - Batching & dynamic scheduling: 10–25% improvement in per-token runtime cost (depends on latency SLOs)
   - Quantization: 5–20% CPU/GPU cost reduction at the potential expense of small quality deltas — should be evaluated per model

5) EU-specific notes:
   - Because you require at-rest and processing residency in EU, there is an operational premium (in-region capacity + compliance controls). We apply the regional premium above; there may also be one-time onboarding/security review fees for Private deployment if you choose that path.
   - Egress: if any data crosses regions for analytics or backups, there may be additional egress fees; we recommend keeping analytics in-region where possible.

Next steps:
- If this looks reasonable, propose: 30-min align with procurement + technical ops early next week to finalize pilot SOW and commit term.
- If procurement needs a formal quote/PO line items, we'll generate an official quote after the short call.

Thanks — I've attached the SOW-draft.pdf and the updated pricing-model.xlsx for your review.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
